channel.title: Overnight Brief
channel.description: A private daily audio digest of the strongest insights from the overnight newsletters. Built for one listener.
channel.itunes:author: Rohit
channel.itunes:summary: A private daily audio digest of the strongest insights from the overnight newsletters.

item.title: Ep 16: When the Customer Is a Machine
item.description: Why software agents are becoming customers and what a bits-perfect transaction stack requires; Kae Capital's 18x partial exit from Nua; how cheap models move value into physical learning systems; AI safety's culture-war problem; India's regional PE deal tape; and defense tech's distribution incentives.

item.title: Ep 15: Anthropic's Half-Trillion-Dollar Power Bill
item.description: Anthropic's potential $1.5 trillion IPO and up to $517 billion of compute commitments; whether AI labs can police themselves; how Engram moves learned memory from HBM to DRAM; Salesforce yielding the interface to general assistants; and the geopolitical and financial fault lines beneath AI infrastructure.

item.title: Ep 14: Ten Thousand Agents and One Broken Lock
item.description: OpenAI's 10,000-agent, 130-billion-token Navier-Stokes run and what it says about recursive self-improvement; the shared skill-update flaw across four leading coding agents; Bridgewater's call to regulate compute giants like systemic banks; the publisher doom loop; and OpenAI's next private round at a possible $1.2 trillion valuation.

item.title: Ep 13: Compute Needs a Down Payment
item.description: The Fed hike meets AI project finance: GPU prepayments, customer-credit spreads and guarantees; Apollo moves private credit into venture-backed hardware; Apple considers M8 Ultra enterprise servers linked by Nvidia NVLink Fusion; Zipline seeks $1 billion at a $20 billion valuation; and why cost of capital per usable token is the metric beneath the boom.

item.title: Ep 12: Count Megawatts, Not Moratoriums
item.description: Why 300-plus local data-centre restrictions translate into only 1,525 MW of actual delay, how behind-the-meter power changes the winners, OpenAI's agentic software factory and the shift from code generation to verification, enterprise zero-data-retention as a model-market weapon, Meta's camera-free Luna glasses, and why AI subscriptions must earn permission to charge.

item.title: Ep 11: The Speed Limit Becomes a Business Model
item.description: Vera Rubin NVL72 and what its 67x headline really means for agentic inference, KV cache, mixture-of-experts routing, total cost and power; AI leaders ask for a speed limit and markets price safety risk; why regulation solves a coordination problem while protecting incumbents; on-device versus data-centre inference; and the $10B Kioxia ADR and $29.6B ByteDance loan show the capital stack following the rack.

item.title: Ep 10: Amodei Pulls the Brake, the Labs Build Their Own Referee, and the Memory Wall Breaks
item.description: Amodei's Saturday essay calls for an industry slowdown and Altman, Musk, and Trump all react within hours; OpenAI's IPO slips to 2027; The Information reveals Anthropic, OpenAI, and Google were already discussing a self-policing standards body; SemiAnalysis reverses the HBM stack race (4-hi wins, Rubin Ultra downgrades to 192GB); Nvidia's filings show three customers at 44% of sales; the $110M Frederick community deal buys the buildout its politics; and two dozen mathematicians formally warn AI could ruin the foundations of maths.

item.title: Ep 9: Pixxel's $100M Weekend, India's Exit Machine Wakes Up, and Robots vs the Treasury Market
item.description: Pixxel closes the largest round in Indian spacetech ($100M, Temasek + Seraphim) while ISRO staff push back on privatization, India's exit machine prints receipts (Kae's 18x on Nua, Circle buying Tazapay for $400M, Kotak's 2x toll road), the WSJ declares America's Great AI Freakout, Bloomberg asks if robots are ruining the Treasury market with high yields here to stay and $6 diesel, the US links Chinese satellite imagery to a deadly Iranian strike ahead of the Trump-Xi summit, sudden wealth syndrome hits tech's new rich, StarCraft is back while Xbox bleeds, and the FSSAI wants warning labels on your snacks.

item.title: Ep 8: The Fed Blinks at $120 Oil, Nvidia's $530B Shadow Balance Sheet, and the Sanity Caucus
item.description: CPI at 3.4% and futures at 85% for the first Fed hike in three years as the Saudi East-West pipeline shuts and Houthis squeeze Bab al-Mandeb, Brent over $104 with $120 calls, SemiAnalysis maps Nvidia's $530B of off-balance-sheet backstops, Schulman and friends debate recursive self-improvement, the sanity caucus pushes back on extinction math, Instinct's own compute crunch makes the news, and Salesforce vs Figma on whether the UI is dead.

item.title: Ep 7: Oracle's Prepayment Machine, the Sandbox Is Leaking, and Crude Tops $109
item.description: Oracle's 30% growth and the $11.4B customer-prepayment engine financing the AI buildout, OpenAI suspending Pro subs on Astra demand, Jacob Coxon's exit going mainstream plus Anthropic's hotel-Wi-Fi hacking report, the leaky sandboxes inside Claude Code/Codex/Cursor, the $7.5T financing stack and Blackstone's bid, Burry shorting the dollar over quantum, and crude topping $109.

item.title: Ep 6: iPhone Duo Day, Anthropic's Extinction Number, and Where a Robot Thinks
item.description: John Ternus unfolds the $1,999 iPhone Duo and throws down the Siri Recap gauntlet, an Anthropic researcher quits with a 10% extinction warning weeks before the IPO roadshow, OpenAI's agents solve a decades-old math problem while pulling up the drawbridge on Adobe and six Chinese labs, SemiAnalysis on where a robot thinks, Lightfield's $47M Tome redemption arc, and Levine's AAA AI catastrophe-bond warning.

item.title: Ep 5: OpenAI Starts a Price War, Data Beat the Architects, and iPhone Fold Day Is Here
item.description: OpenAI cuts Luna prices and takes the model war to Anthropic's IPO math, Dwarkesh's data-vs-architecture study (12x vs 3.7x), Matt Levine on tokenized AMC, iPhone Fold day and Ternus tonight, Hugging Face's robotics push, a Grok Bot built in a month, agent-era code review, Chime buys Stride for $590M, and Brent over $99 after tanker strikes.

item.title: Ep 4: The TPU Goes Outside, Data Centers Call the Shots, and Apple's Foldable Eve
item.description: SemiAnalysis's first third-party TPUv7 Ironwood benchmarks (up to 50% better perf/dollar than B200), the data-center SLA power flip, Apple's foldable eve with Ternus's first keynote tomorrow, G42/ByteDance/Humain statecraft, the yen's breakout, and Claire's OpenClaw-to-Grok-Bot agent migration.

item.title: Special: The Invisible Layer - What Astra Isn't Saying, and the Jobs That Never Show Up
item.description: Deep-dive special. Act 1: OpenAI's Astra and the recurrent-depth fight - what the architecture actually is, the monitorability scare, and the twist that both sides co-wrote the warning. Act 2: the jobs data - The Economist's one-million-jobs case vs Stanford's 19% young-worker gap, codified vs tacit knowledge, and what it all means for India's $315B IT services industry.

item.title: Ep 3: Anthropic Meets the S-1, Oura's Victory Lap, and the Rise of the Robot Retail Investor
item.description: Anthropic's IPO housekeeping and Cognition's $900M burn rate, Oura's profitable S-1, retail investors vibe-coding quant funds, the AI jobs apocalypse postponed, Cook's $47M chairman package, Tether's $42M freeze lawsuit, and companies as loops.

item.title: Special: Six Months of Stratechery - Agents Ate the Chatbot, Compute Became an Asset Class, and the Gatekeepers Fell
item.description: A 30-minute two-host deep dive: 115 Stratechery emails from March to September 2026 distilled into the six themes that mattered - agents ending the bubble debate, compute as an asset class, Anthropic's safety superpower, the end of Apple's Cook era, China's commoditization battle, and the fall of the gatekeepers.

item.title: Ep 2 (Two-Host Edition): Astra's Hidden Loops, Nvidia Buys the Stadium, and the End of the Cook Era
item.description: The new format: two hosts, one conversation. OpenAI's Astra and the recurrent depth rumor, Anthropic's three-act week, Nvidia's $12.9B Hugging Face deal, Tim Cook hands Apple to John Ternus, a loaded India package, ShieldFont vs the scrapers, Qualcomm's 40 AI devices, and the a16z charts that matter.

item.title: Ep 1 (Demo): Astra's Hidden Loops, Anthropic's Reality Check, and the End of the Cook Era
item.description: The original demo: single-host brief from the Friday night newsletters.
